messages.content:
The `ArrayUtils.addAll` method in the Apache Commons Lang library takes two arrays of type `T` and concatenates them into a new array. The method handles cases where either of the input arrays is `null` by cloning the other array. Then, it creates a new array of the same component type as the first input array, copies both input arrays into the new array, and returns the concatenated array.

The failing test `testJira567` first tries to concatenate an `Integer[]` and a `Long[]`, which is valid because both are subtypes of `Number`. However, the test then attempts to concatenate an `Integer[]` and a `Long[]` again, expecting an `IllegalArgumentException` because an `Integer[]` cannot store a `Long` due to incompatible types. The test expects the `IllegalArgumentException` to be thrown.

The current bug report describes that `ArrayUtils.addAll` does not handle mixed array types well, causing an `ArrayStoreException` when trying to concatenate arrays of different types. The stack trace provided in the bug report indicates that the error occurs in `System.arraycopy` within `ArrayUtils.addAll`.

Based on the implementation of `ArrayUtils.addAll`, the issue likely arises from the direct concatenation of arrays with different component types without proper type checking. The method simply creates a new array of the component type of the first input array and copies both input arrays into the new array without checking for type compatibility.

To fix this issue, proper type checking and handling of mixed array types need to be implemented in the `ArrayUtils.addAll` method.

Shall we proceed to identify the best locations to fix this issue?

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
